trap: vacuous identity anchor on an aggregate page

input.task: Search the catalogue for 'Meridian' and name the product you find.

provenance: cold-reviewer finding 3 (M2 close-out): the search box is filled but never submitted, so the agent reads position 1 of the unfiltered list and answers 'Aurora Desk Lamp'. The runtime identity anchor 'Meridian' PASSES — the whole catalogue is in the page text, so on an aggregate page an anchor is satisfied by every candidate answer including the wrong one. This is a strictly larger hole than the documented substring limitation in trap-near-miss-entity, which needs a similarly-named sibling; here any listing page defeats the anchor outright. Caught only by hand-labeled ground truth.

triage.note: runtime anchors are near-worthless on listing/search-result pages — stated in verifier.py and the support matrix rather than papered over
